method.method_draft: Use a coordinate setup. Read from the diagram that A is the lower-left corner, B lower-right, C upper-right, D upper-left, and that X and Y are the opposite vertices of the two axis-aligned squares. Put A=(0,0), B=(20,0), C=(20,15), D=(0,15). The diagonal BD has equation y=15-(3/4)x. If the square at A has side length s, then X=(s,s), so solve s=15-(3/4)s to get s=60/7. If the square at C has side length t, then Y=(20-t,15-t), so solve 15-t=15-(3/4)(20-t), giving t=60/7. Thus X=(60/7,60/7) and Y=(80/7,45/7). Compute XY by the distance formula: horizontal difference 20/7 and vertical difference 15/7, so XY=sqrt((20/7)^2+(15/7)^2)=25/7.

From the rectangle, BD is a 15-20-25 diagonal, so along BD every horizontal-to-vertical displacement has ratio 4:3 and length scale 5. For the A-square, let its side be s. Since X is the upper-right corner of that square, from B to X the horizontal leftward displacement is 20-s and the vertical upward displacement is s. Because X lies on BD, s/(20-s)=3/4, so s=60/7. Therefore BX=(5/4)(20-s)=100/7. For the C-square, let its side be t. Since Y is the lower-left corner of that square, from B to Y the horizontal leftward displacement is t and the vertical upward displacement is 15-t. Since Y lies on BD, (15-t)/t=3/4, so t=60/7. Therefore BY=(5/4)t=75/7. The condition BX>BY confirms the order B-Y-X-D, so XY=BX-BY=100/7-75/7=25/7.
